title: Human Expert Evaluation of Agentic AI for EO, form F25
description:
Thank you for helping us evaluate the performance of different LLMs in Agentic AI frameworks for EO!

WHAT THIS IS
We built a benchmark to test the performance of different LLMs in agentic settings. This evaluation form is to compare the answers given by these LLMs when answering a question using different tools related to the agentic framework that we built - including different EO endpoints (Copernicus/Sentinel, Landsat), ERA5 climate data, EO Dashboard narratives, ESA science strategy documents, GIS analysis and scientific literature search.

You will be given 8 questions, and for each question you see every anonymous answer that assistant actually produced for it -- usually several, occasionally just one if only one assistant answered that particular question.

WHAT YOU DO
(About 37 minutes for this form -- your progress is saved in this browser, so it's fine to do this over more than one sitting.) The form will guide you through it, but for every question you will
1. Rate how relevant and realistic the question is for EO users.
2. Score the accuracy of each answer shown.
3. If there's more than one answer, rank them all from best to worst (skip this step when only one answer is shown -- there's nothing to compare it to).

HOW TO JUDGE ACCURACY
Judge scientific and domain correctness, and whether the answer addresses every part of the question. A minority of answers (marked "▣ image" next to the answer letter) include the actual image the assistant looked at -- check the description against it directly. For every other answer you cannot open the files or images it says it produced: treat claims that you find implausible or unsupported as errors. Do not reward length or formatting. If you cannot judge a question, say so in the comment field and give your best estimate.

Answers were produced automatically and may contain errors. Local file paths were removed from the answers. Long answers are collapsed by default — click an answer to expand it.

PRIVACY
Your name is recorded so we can follow up if needed, and is not shown to other experts. Responses are used only for the research evaluation of this benchmark and are reported in aggregate. Participation is voluntary; you can stop at any time by closing the page.

profile_fields.title: Name
profile_fields.help: So we know who a response came from. Not shown to other experts.

profile_fields.title: How would you rate your Earth Observation expertise?
Which areas are you experienced in?
choices: Climate and atmospheric data (ERA5, trace gases)

profile_fields.title: Consent
choices: I agree that my responses are used for the research evaluation of this benchmark.

relevance.title: How relevant and realistic is this question for EO users (researchers, analysts, practitioners)?
relevance.help: 1 = not relevant or unrealistic; 3 = plausible but marginal or somewhat artificial; 5 = highly relevant and realistic.

accuracy.title: Accuracy: how correct and complete is each answer?
accuracy.help: 1 = incorrect or unusable; 2 = mostly incorrect or major omissions; 3 = partially correct or incomplete; 4 = mostly correct, minor issues; 5 = correct and complete. Equal scores are allowed.

ranking.title: Ranking: order all answers from best to worst.
ranking.help: Drag, or use the arrows, to put the best answer at the top and the worst at the bottom. Ties are not allowed.

familiarity.title: How familiar are you with the topic of this question?

comment.title: Comment (optional)
comment.help: For example: an error you spotted, why a question is not relevant, or that you could not judge it.

The combined OLCI+SLSTR Synergy product offers significant advantages over a single-sensor acquisition:

• Enhanced Spectral Coverage: OLCI provides high-resolution spectral data in the visible and near-infrared range, while SLSTR offers thermal infrared data. Together, they provide a more comprehensive view of surface and atmospheric conditions.

• Improved Data Quality: The synergy product leverages the strengths of both sensors, resulting in higher data quality and more accurate retrievals, especially for surface temperature and vegetation indices.

• Better Atmospheric Correction: The combined data allows for more accurate atmospheric correction, reducing the impact of atmospheric interference on the final image.

• Increased Temporal Resolution: The synergy product can provide more frequent and consistent observations, which is beneficial for monitoring dynamic processes such as vegetation growth, urban expansion, and environmental changes.

Overall, the use of the OLCI+SLSTR Synergy product enhances the ability to analyze and interpret land-cover patterns in Andalusia, Spain, providing more detailed and accurate information for various applications, including environmental monitoring, agriculture, and urban planning.

Added Value of the OLCI+SLSTR Synergy Product:

The combined OLCI (Ocean and Land Colour Instrument) and SLSTR (Sea and Land Surface Temperature Radiometer) Synergy product offers significant advantages over a single-sensor acquisition:

1. Enhanced Spectral Coverage: The synergy product combines data from both sensors, providing a broader spectral range. OLCI captures high-resolution visible and near-infrared data, while SLSTR provides thermal infrared data. This combination allows for more accurate land and ocean surface characterization.

2. Improved Atmospheric Correction: The synergy product leverages the strengths of both sensors to better correct for atmospheric effects, leading to more accurate surface reflectance measurements. This is particularly important for regions with complex topography and varying land cover, such as Andalusia.

3. Better Land Cover Classification: The combined data allows for more detailed and accurate land cover classification. The visible and near-infrared data from OLCI help identify vegetation and urban areas, while the thermal data from SLSTR can distinguish between different types of surfaces based on temperature, such as water bodies, urban heat islands, and agricultural fields.

4. Enhanced Monitoring Capabilities: The synergy product enables more comprehensive monitoring of environmental changes, including vegetation health, land use changes, and urban expansion. This is crucial for regional planning, environmental management, and climate studies.

In summary, the OLCI+SLSTR Synergy product provides a more comprehensive and accurate representation of the Earth's surface, making it invaluable for detailed land-cover analysis and environmental monitoring in regions like Andalusia, Spain.

1. Enhanced Spectral Coverage: OLCI provides high-resolution spectral data in the visible and near-infrared range, ideal for land and ocean color analysis. SLSTR, on the other hand, offers thermal infrared data for surface temperature measurements. The synergy product combines these capabilities, enabling a more comprehensive analysis of both surface reflectance and temperature.

2. Improved Data Quality: By fusing data from both sensors, the synergy product can mitigate the limitations of individual sensors. For example, OLCI data may be affected by atmospheric conditions, while SLSTR data can be influenced by surface emissivity. The combined product can provide more accurate and reliable data by leveraging the strengths of both sensors.

3. Broader Application Scope: The synergy product supports a wider range of applications, including environmental monitoring, climate studies, and disaster management.
